title: Input memory condition
statement: Let $W$ be a word size, let $\mathrm{lim}$ be a triple of resource limits, let $\mu\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ assign an integer to each natural-numbered address, and let $m\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\{0,1\}^W$ be a memory of $W$-bit words. For integers $i$ and $j$, the input condition requires that $m(a)=\mathrm{wd}_W(\mu(a))$ and $|\mu(a)|\leq\mathrm{lim.word}$ for every natural number $a$, that the memory cells at the first and second argument addresses encode $i$ and $j$, respectively, and that $|i|,|j|\leq\mathrm{lim.word}$.
hypotheses_covered: Memory $m$ of $W$-bit words indexed by integers
Every natural-numbered cell represents $\mu(a)$ and satisfies the word bound
Both arguments satisfy the word bound
